"'''How Deep Is Your Love'''" is a [[Sentimental ballad|ballad]] written and recorded by the [[Bee Gees]] in 1977 and released as a single in September of that year by [[RSO Records]]. It was later used as part of the film ''[[Saturday Night Fever]]''{{'}}s [[Saturday Night Fever (soundtrack)|soundtrack]]. It was a number-three hit in the United Kingdom and Australia. In the United States, it topped the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] on 25 December 1977 and stayed in the Top 10 for 17 weeks. It spent six weeks atop the US [[Hot Adult Contemporary Tracks|adult contemporary chart]]. It is 27th on ''Billboard''{{'s}} All Time Top 100.<ref name="Bronson 7">{{cite magazine|url= http://www.billboard.com/articles/list/2155531/the-hot-100-all-time-top-songs?list_page=7 |title= Hot 100 55th Anniversary: The All-Time Top 100 Songs |magazine= Billboard |date= 2 August 2012 |access-date= 9 August 2013 |first= Fred |last= Bronson}}</ref> Alongside "[[Stayin' Alive]]" and "[[Night Fever]]", it is one of the group's three tracks on the list. [[Take That]]'s recording of the song for their 1996 ''[[Greatest Hits (Take That album)|Greatest Hits]]'' album reached No. 1 on the [[UK Singles Chart]] for three weeks.<ref name="British Hit Singles & Albums">{{cite book | first= David | last= Roberts | year= 2006 | title= [[British Hit Singles & Albums]] | edition= 19th | publisher= Guinness World Records Limited  | location= London | isbn= 1-904994-10-5 | page= 591}}</ref>

"How Deep Is Your Love" ranked 375th on ''[[Rolling Stone]]''{{'s}} list of the [[500 Greatest Songs of All Time]]. In a 2011 British TV special, ITV viewers voted it [[The Nation's Favourite|The Nation's Favourite Bee Gees Song]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.itv.com/beegees/ |title=ITV |publisher=ITV.com |access-date=31 March 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121019120053/http://www.itv.com/beegees/ |archive-date=19 October 2012 }}</ref> In the Bee Gees' 2001 ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine interview, [[Barry Gibb|Barry]] said it was his favourite Bee Gees song.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WxQEAAAAMBAJ&q=bee+gees+this+is+where+i+came+in&pg=PA58 |title=The Bee Gees: 35 Years of Music |magazine=Billboard |date=24 March 2001 |page=27 |access-date=12 February 2015}}</ref>

sections.heading: Composition and recording
sections.wikitext:
{{Listen | type = music | filename = HowDeepIsYourLove.ogg | title = "How Deep Is Your Love" sample }} After mixing ''[[Here at Last... Bee Gees... Live]]'', the Bee Gees began recording songs for the followup studio album to 1976's ''[[Children of the World]]''. Then their manager Robert Stigwood requested songs for a movie he was producing. The Bee Gees obliged with five songs, one of which was "How Deep Is Your Love". Barry worked out the structure for the melody with keyboard player [[Blue Weaver]]. Co-producer [[Albhy Galuten]] later admitted Weaver's contribution, calling it a song "where Blue had a tremendous amount of input. There was a lot of things from his personality. That's one where his contribution was quite significant, not in a songwriting sense, though when you play piano, it's almost like writing the song. Blue had a lot of influence in the piano structure of that song".{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Uzv_AgAAQBAJ&q=bee+gees+book |title=The Bee Gees |author1=Melinda Bilyeu |author2=Hector Cook |author3=Andrew Môn Hughes |date=January 2011 |publisher=Omnibus Press |isbn=9780857128942 |access-date=9 February 2015}} Weaver said:
One morning, it was just myself and Barry in the studio. He said, "Play the most beautiful chord you know" and I just played—what happened was, I'd throw chords at him and he'd say, "No, not that chord," and I'd keep moving around and he'd say, "Yeah, that's a nice one" and we'd go from there. Then I'd play another thing—sometimes I'd be following the melody line that he already had and sometimes I'd most probably lead him somewhere else by doing what I did. I think Robin came in at some point. Albhy also came in at one point and I was playing an inversion of a chord, and he said, "Oh no, I don't think it should be that inversion, it should be this," and so we changed it to that, but by the time Albhy had come in, the song was sort of there.
A demo was made at [[Château d'Hérouville|Le Château d'Hérouville]] in France, with additional recording done at [[Criteria Studios]] in Miami.{{cite web|url=http://www.columbia.edu/~brennan/beegees/77.html |title=Gibb Songs: 1977 |publisher=Columbia.edu |date=20 December 1976|access-date=31 March 2014}} Weaver said, "We started work about 12 o'clock—maybe one o'clock in the morning, and that demo was done at about three or four o'clock in the morning. Albhy played piano on the demo. I'd drunk too much or gone to bed or something. Then I woke up the next morning and listened to that, and then put some strings on it and that was it. Then we actually recorded it for real in Criteria. The chords and everything stayed the same. The only thing that changes from that demo is that when we got to Criteria, I worked out the [[electric piano]] part, which became the basis of the song. It was the sound of the piano that makes the feel of that song." Of the song's lyrics, Barry said:
A lot of the textures you hear in the song were added on later. We didn't change any lyrics, mind you, but the way we recorded it was a little different than the way we wrote in the terms of construction—a little different for the better, I think. The title "How Deep Is Your Love" we thought was perfect because of all the connotations involved in that sentence, and that was simply it.
There was some talk of [[Yvonne Elliman]] recording "How Deep Is Your Love", but according to Barry, Stigwood said: "You've got to do this song yourself. You should not give it to anybody".

sections.heading: Release and critical reception
sections.wikitext:
"How Deep Is Your Love" was released as a single in September 1977 in the United States and on 14 October 1977 in the United Kingdom.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Fact sheet|magazine=[[Music Week]]|page=63|date=22 October 1977}}</ref> By the time ''[[Children of the World]]'' was recorded, it had largely been established that Barry was the group's primary vocalist, mostly singing in falsetto and occasionally in a natural breathy voice. He even sang most of the backing vocals; Robin and Maurice are barely heard in the mix. Robin sings the melody in the chorus and various ad libs. Two videos were made for the song, with minimum lights. In one (the precursor to the main video), the brothers are shown singing while a shady image of a woman appears throughout, accompanied by a big white light. Barry is clean-shaven, as in the "[[Night Fever]]" video.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CWZCV7cO_qA  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/CWZCV7cO_qA |archive-date=21 December 2021 |url-status=live|title=1977 Bee Gees – How deep is your love (Alternate Version) |date=18 May 2008 |via=YouTube |access-date=31 March 2014}}{{cbignore}}</ref> In the main video, the brothers sing while passing by a stream of rainbow lights. Barry is bearded. On the ''[[Cashbox (magazine)|Cashbox]]'' charts for 4 February 1978, when it was at No. 13, the soundtrack's second single, "[[Stayin' Alive]]", was at No. 1. "Night Fever" debuted at No. 71 on the same week.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cashboxmagazine.com/archives/70s_files/19780204.html |title=Cashbox Top 100 Singles |date=7 February 1964 |publisher=Cashbox Archives |access-date=10 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121004090240/http://cashboxmagazine.com/archives/70s_files/19780204.html |archive-date=4 October 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

When "How Deep Is Your Love" reached No. 3 in the UK, Barry said: "You have no idea what a thrill it is to have a Top Five single in England. With all the [[new wave music|new wave]] and [[punk rock]] out, I would have thought something like 'How Deep Is Your Love' wouldn't have a chance. We always kept going forward and we're getting stronger every day".<ref name="piano"/>

''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' called the song "a warm tender ballad", saying that after a slow beginning it grows to a "heightened expressive delivery."<ref>{{cite news|title=Top Single Picks|newspaper=Billboard|access-date=11 July 2020|page=64|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-Billboard/70s/1977/Billboard%201977-09-24.pdf|date=24 September 1977}}</ref> ''[[Cash Box]]'' called it "a beautifully harmonized, melodic ballad for music lovers of all ages."<ref name=cb>{{cite news|title=CashBox Singles Reviews|date=24 September 1977|page=24|newspaper=Cashbox|accessdate=26 December 2021|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Cash-Box/70s/1977/CB-1977-09-24.pdf}}</ref> ''[[Record World]]'' called it "one of their most controlled, delicate efforts, with the vocals almost whispered at times", adding that it has "a good melody and expressive love lyric".<ref name=rw>{{cite magazine|magazine=Record World|date=24 September 1977|accessdate=16 February 2023|title=Hits of the Week|page=1|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Record-World/70s/77/Record-World-1977-09-24.pdf}}</ref>

[[Allmusic]] critic Bill Janovitz praised the "sublimely gorgeous" and "impossibly lovely and memorable classic" melody, as well as Barry's vocal performance.<ref name=allmusic>{{cite web|title=Hoe Deep Is Your Love?|author=Janovitz, Bill|publisher=Allmusic|accessdate=2026-02-09|url=https://www.allmusic.com/song/how-deep-is-your-love--mt0045196991}}</ref> Janovtiz felt that even though the song was released during the Bee Gees' disco period, it has more in common with their late 1960's/early 1970's hits, using "the same sort of heartbreaking major-to minor chord changes and easygoing R&B groove of such nuggets as '[[To Love Somebody (Bee Gees song)|To Love Somebody]],' '[[How Can You Mend a Broken Heart]],' and '[[I've Gotta Get a Message to You]].'"<ref name=allmusic/> 

The song won [[Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals|Best Pop Performance by a Group]] at the 20th Grammy Awards on 23 February 1978. It was also nominated for [[Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song|Best Original Song]] at the 35th Golden Globe awards on 28 January 1978. The award went to [[Joseph Brooks (songwriter)|Joe Brooks]]'s "[[You Light Up My Life (song)|You Light Up My Life]]". During both award ceremonies, the song was in the Top 10 on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Billboard Hot 100|Hot 100]] chart.

[[Brian Wilson]] said of the song: "I always liked the Bee Gees very much. 'How Deep Is Your Love' is [...] one that I think is really great [...] I turn the radio up a little bit when it comes on."<ref name="as brian wilson">{{cite web |last1=Sharp |first1=Ken |title=Brian Wilson: God's Messenger - Page 4 of 5 |url=https://americansongwriter.com/brian-wilson-gods-messenger/4/ |website=American Songwriter |access-date=23 July 2022 |date=2 January 2009}}</ref>

sections.wikitext:
{{Main|Selle v. Gibb}}
In 1983, the Chicago songwriter Ronald Selle sued the Bee Gees, claiming that the Gibb brothers stole melodic material from his song "Let It End" and used it in "How Deep Is Your Love". The jury found for Selle. The Bee Gees' attorney immediately asked for [[judgment notwithstanding the verdict]]. The basis for the motion was that Selle had failed to show, as required by law, that the Bee Gees had access to his song. Selle had said that he had sent the demo tape to only a few recording companies, none of which did business with the Bee Gees. He also admitted that there were some similarities between his song and several Bee Gee songs that predated his song, as well as similarities to the [[The Beatles|Beatles]] song "[[From Me to You]]", by [[John Lennon]] and [[Paul McCartney]] (under [[Lennon-McCartney]]). The federal judge ruled in the Bee Gees' favour. Selle appealed, but the appellate court upheld the ruling, agreeing that Selle had not proven his case.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://law.justia.com/cases/federal/appellate-courts/F2/741/896/90728/ |title=741 F.2d 896: Ronald H. English pop music group [[Take That]] released a cover version as a single from its 1996 ''[[Greatest Hits (Take That album)|Greatest Hits]]'' compilation on [[RCA Records]]. It was the band's first single as a quartet, as [[Robbie Williams]] had left the band the previous year. The band's cover version is exactly the same as the original with the lyrics "I know your eyes in the morning sun, I feel you touch me in the pouring rain" changed to "and when you rise in the morning sun, I feel you touch my hand in the pouring rain" and "I really mean to learn" changed to "I really need to learn".

The single was produced by the band with Chris Porter and became the band's final UK number one until its 2006 comeback single "[[Patience (Take That song)|Patience]]". It was at number one in the UK charts for three weeks. It sold 671,000 copies and has a Platinum sales status certification in the UK. The song also topped the charts in Denmark, Israel, Ireland, Lithuania, and Spain.

In 2018, the band re-recorded an updated version of the song with [[Barry Gibb]] for its [[greatest hits album|greatest hits]] [[remix album]], ''[[Odyssey (Take That album)|Odyssey]]''.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: ''[[Music Week]]'' rated the song three out of five, writing, "This difficult-to-sing Bee Gees number lacks some oomph in this version, which is released as a preview for Take That's forthcoming greatest hits album. A hit, of course, but not one of their biggest."<ref>{{cite magazine|title= Reviews: Singles |magazine= [[Music Week]] |date= 17 February 1996 |page= 12 |accessdate= 23 May 2021 |url= https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-Week/1996/Music-Week-1996-02-17.pdf}}</ref> Gerald Martinez of ''[[New Sunday Times]]'' wrote that it sounds very much like the original, but that "most of their fans have probably not heard the Bee Gees' version. In any case it's a stylish ballad that deserves another hearing."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Gerald|last=Martinez|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nAFZAAAAIBAJ|title=Lending local voices to Disney hits|magazine=[[New Sunday Times]]|date=21 April 1996|page=16|accessdate=21 October 2021}}</ref> Gina Morris from ''[[Smash Hits]]'' rated it five out of five and named it Best New Single, writing, "this is a fitting reminder of the good old times. An unplugged smoochy bongo-buoy [[disco]] record, originally recorded by the Bee Gees in the gruesome '70s for the movie ''[[Saturday Night Fever]]''. Taken from their forthcoming ''Greatest Hits - Volume 1'', it's a great choice of song—tampered with, but not totally destroyed."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Gina|last=Morris|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/smashhits90s/32791504020/in/album-72157677432333053/|title=Singles|magazine=[[Smash Hits]]|date=28 February 1996|page=54|access-date=1 December 2024}}</ref>

sections.heading: Video
sections.wikitext:
The video for "How Deep Is Your Love" was directed by English photographer [[Nick Brandt]] and shot on 7 and 8 February at a deserted warehouse and by a reservoir in [[Hayes, Hillingdon|Hayes]], [[Middlesex]].<ref name="smashhits">{{cite magazine|first=|last=|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/smashhits90s/33132297006/in/album-72157677432333053|title=How Deep Is Your Loch?|magazine=[[Smash Hits]]|date=28 February 1996|page=14|access-date=1 December 2024}}</ref> It was filmed six days before the band's breakup was announced and depicts the remaining four members tied to chairs in a basement.

An obsessive fan ([[Paula Hamilton]])<ref name="smashhits" /> with blonde hair and heavy eye makeup who has presumably kidnapped the band walks into the basement and circles the four members, pulling their hair. She puts them all into a van and drives down the motorway. She stops by a reservoir and has the four members placed on the edge, pointing at each before grabbing [[Gary Barlow]]'s rope and pushing him back, still holding on. Her fingers slip through the rope and he falls into the reservoir, still tied to the chair. She initially looks shocked, then smirks. [[MTV Europe]] cut some scenes of the video.

sections.heading: Other notable versions
sections.wikitext:
* In 1978, Italian singer [[Peppino di Capri]] recorded an Italian-language version titled ''Fiore di carta'' (Splash, SPH 1030), included on the album ''Verdemela'' (Splash, SPL 713).
*[[Luther Vandross]]'s cover of "How Deep Is Your Love" from his 1993 album ''[[Never Let Me Go (Luther Vandross album)|Never Let Me Go]]'' was nominated for [[Grammy Award for Best Male R&B Vocal Performance|Best Male R&B Vocal Performance]] at the [[36th Grammy Awards]] in 1994.{{cn|date=November 2025}}
*American R&B group [[Portrait (group)|Portrait]] included a version on its album ''[[All That Matters (Portrait album)|All That Matters]]'' and released it as a single on 23 May 1995.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Selected New Releases|magazine=[[Radio & Records]]|issue=1095|pages=31, 37|date=19 May 1995}}</ref> The single reached No. 93 on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100,<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/portrait |title=Portrait Billboard Chart History - Hot 100|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=18 August 2019}}</ref> No. 15 in Australia,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://australian-charts.com/showitem.asp?interpret=Portrait+%5BUS%5D&titel=How+Deep+Is+Your+Love&cat=s |title=australian-charts.com - Portrait - How Deep Is Your Love|website=australian-charts.com|publisher=Hung Medien|access-date=18 August 2019}}</ref> and No. 1 in New Zealand for three weeks,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://charts.nz/showitem.asp?interpret=Portrait+%5BUS%5D&titel=How+Deep+Is+Your+Love&cat=s|title=charts.nz - Portrait - How Deep Is Your Love |website=charts.nz|publisher=Hung Medien|access-date=18 August 2019}}</ref> where it was certified gold<ref>{{cite certification|region=New Zealand|type=single|title=How Deep Is Your Love|id=1995-11-03|source=newchart|access-date=20 November 2024|artist=Portrait}}</ref> and ranked No. 6 on the year-end singles chart.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://aotearoamusiccharts.co.nz/archive/annual-singles/1995-12-31|title=The Official NZ Music Charts - End of Year Charts 1995|publisher=[[Recorded Music NZ]]|access-date=18 August 2019}}</ref>
*A [[Muzak]] version of this song played at the [[Austin J. Tobin Plaza]] of the [[World Trade Center (1973–2001)|World Trade Center]] during the [[September 11 attacks]], as observed in footage recorded by Jack Taliercio. The song plays as the Twin Towers burn.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qu5UKC4ASdk |title= 9/11 Jack Taliercio World Trade Center Plaza Footage Released in 2010 |website=youtube.com|date= 12 December 2011 |access-date=14 October 2023}}</ref>
* New Zealand duo [[Adeaze]] covered the song for their 2004 album ''Always and for Real''. In 2020, it was certified gold by [[Recorded Music NZ]] (RMNZ).<ref>{{Cite certification|type=single|region=New Zealand|title=How Deep Is Your Love?|artist=Adeaze|source=radioscope|access-date=21 August 2025}}</ref>
*[[Lionel Loueke]] recorded the song on his 2015 album ''[[Gaïa (album)|Gaïa]]''.<ref name="AM">{{cite web |last1=Jurek |first1=Thom |title=Gaïa - Lionel Loueke {{!}} Album {{!}} AllMusic |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/ga%C3%AFa-mw0002881637 |publisher=[[AllMusic]] |access-date=13 December 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="AAJ">{{cite web |last1=Turner |first1=Mark F. |title=Lionel Loueke: GAïA album review @ All About Jazz |url=https://www.allaboutjazz.com/gaia-lionel-loueke-blue-note-records-review-by-mark-f-turner |website=[[All About Jazz]] |access-date=13 December 2025 |language=en |date=25 October 2015}}</ref>
*[[PJ Morton]] released a version on his 2017 album ''Gumbo'', featuring [[Yebba]]. The song won a [[Grammy Award for Best Traditional R&B Performance]].{{citation needed|date=November 2022}}
*A cover of the song features in the 2024 film ''[[Kinds of Kindness]]'', performed by [[Margaret Qualley]]'s character, Vivian.<ref>{{Citation |title=Margaret Qualley – How Deep Is Your Love |url=https://genius.com/Margaret-qualley-how-deep-is-your-love-lyrics |access-date=2 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jacob |first=Lola |date=25 June 2024 |title=Margaret Qualley covers 'How Deep Is Your Love' for Yorgos Lanthimos' 'Kinds of Kindness'. |url=https://www.coupdemainmagazine.com/margaret-qualley/19769 |access-date=2 September 2024 |website=Coup De Main Magazine |language=en}}</ref>
*American singer [[Prince Royce]] released a [[Bachata (music)|bachata]] cover of the song on 10 April 2025 as the lead single from his first covers album, ''Eterno''.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://entertainment-focus.com/2025/04/11/prince-royce-puts-a-new-spin-on-how-deep-is-your-love/|title=Prince Royce puts a new spin on 'How Deep Is Your Love'|last=Ellwood-Hughes|first=Pip|date=11 April 2025|access-date=10 June 2025|magazine=Entertainment Focus |language=en }}</ref> It debuted at numbers eight and six on the US [[Hot Tropical Songs]] and Tropical Airplay charts, respectively, becoming his 36th top-10 entry on the latter.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Bustios|first=Pamela|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/prince-royce-tropical-airplay-how-deep-is-your-love-1235953323/|title=Prince Royce Notches 36th Top 10 on Tropical Airplay with Bilingual Bachata 'How Deep Is Your Love'|date=23 April 2025|access-date=10 June 2025|magazine=Billboard}}</ref>

*Luther Vandross's cover of "How Deep Is Your Love" from his 1993 album Never Let Me Go was nominated for Best Male R&B Vocal Performance at the 36th Grammy Awards in 1994.{{cn|date=November 2025}}
*American R&B group Portrait included a version on its album All That Matters and released it as a single on 23 May 1995. The single reached No. 93 on the Billboard Hot 100, No. 15 in Australia, and No. 1 in New Zealand for three weeks, where it was certified gold and ranked No. 6 on the year-end singles chart.
*A Muzak version of this song played at the Austin J. Tobin Plaza of the World Trade Center during the September 11 attacks, as observed in footage recorded by Jack Taliercio. The song plays as the Twin Towers burn.
* New Zealand duo Adeaze covered the song for their 2004 album Always and for Real. In 2020, it was certified gold by Recorded Music NZ (RMNZ).
*Lionel Loueke recorded the song on his 2015 album Gaïa.
*PJ Morton released a version on his 2017 album Gumbo, featuring Yebba. The song won a Grammy Award for Best Traditional R&B Performance.{{citation needed|date=November 2022}}
*A cover of the song features in the 2024 film Kinds of Kindness, performed by Margaret Qualley's character, Vivian.
*American singer Prince Royce released a bachata cover of the song on 10 April 2025 as the lead single from his first covers album, Eterno. It debuted at numbers eight and six on the US Hot Tropical Songs and Tropical Airplay charts, respectively, becoming his 36th top-10 entry on the latter.
